pipeline.name: weekly-infrastructure-health
pipeline.description: Weekly Infrastructure Health pipeline — deep audit of external + internal + container state, with historical context

parent.title: [{{date}}] Weekly Infrastructure Health
description: Replaces (paused) Weekly Docker Image Update Check. Note: External Health Check (3x daily uptime ping) and Internal Health Check (daily) remain standalone — different scope.
This pipeline runs Wednesday 09:00. Goal: deep weekly audit beyond daily uptime, with memory of past incidents.
## Your responsibilities (you're sole owner — Founding Engineer runs all steps)
1. read-history → 2. external-audit → 3. internal-audit → 4. update-check → 5. synthesize → 6. execute → 7. write-history
Critical issues = urgent issues created immediately. Moderate = batched into a single weekly issue.
- Do NOT post status comments like 'I'm starting' or 'I'm blocked' — the task status (`todo`/`in_progress`/`blocked`/`done`) already conveys this.
- Each step posts EXACTLY ONE comment: the structured output. The same comment also @mentions the next agent if applicable.
- Orchestrator (you, when applicable) consolidates verification + transition + @mention next agent into ONE comment per handoff.
- The parent task gets at most 2 comments per run: 'pipeline started' (optional) and final summary at close.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Infra Health — Read history
description: ## Pull past 90 days of infrastructure interventions
node scripts/tools/pipeline-memory.mjs recall weekly-infrastructure-health 'incidents, infra changes, recurring issues, Docker updates, SSL/DNS' --limit 12 --days 90

**If recall exits non-zero**: do NOT block the pipeline. Instead, post a warning comment ('Memory recall failed: <error>. Proceeding without historical context for this run.') and continue with the rest of the steps using only current data. Only block the pipeline if the WRITE step (last task) fails — that's where we'd lose this run's learning forever. Exit codes: 3 = Ollama unavailable (most common, transient), 2 = network/auth (catastrophic, escalate to Founding Engineer).
- Recurring issues (same alert >2x in past 90 days)
- Recent interventions (Docker updates, SSL renewals, DNS changes)
- Open items still waiting for action
- **Last week's memory ID** (you'll update its `outcome:` tag in step 7 based on what you observe today vs what was predicted)
Post recall + summary as comment. Set task to done.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Infra Health — External audit
description: Capture: uptime, SSL expiry days, DNS records, sitemap validity, RSS validity, broken links count, Cloudflare Pages deploy status, SEOnaut critical/moderate counts.
Post a comment with structured findings. Set task to done.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Infra Health — Internal audit
description: psql -U luca -d paperclip -c "SELECT count(*) FROM issues WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days';"
Capture: Docker container statuses, disk usage %, memory pressure, Paperclip service uptime, DB issue volume.
Flag CRITICAL: any service down, disk >85%, memory >90%, Paperclip unresponsive.
Flag MODERATE: disk 75-85%, memory 80-90%, container restart > 1/day.
Post structured comment. Set task to done.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Infra Health — Docker image update check
description: ## Check upstream Docker images for self-hosted services
Services: serpbear, mautic, postiz, seonaut, umami, searxng.
test -f /home/luca/superdots-infra/scripts/check-docker-image-update.mjs || { echo 'SKIP: check script not found'; exit 0; }
for svc in serpbear mautic postiz seonaut umami searxng; do
For each service: log local digest vs remote digest, local image age, recommended update command.
Flag for action only services where: needs_update=true AND local image >30 days old.
Post comment with table of all services + status. Set task to done.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Infra Health — Synthesize + triage
description: ## Triage all findings into action buckets
Read all 3 audit comments. Cross-reference with [{{read_history.identifier}}] (especially: recurring issues).
## Recurring (mentioned in past memory + still present)

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Infra Health — Create action issues
description: For each CRITICAL: create separate issue, priority=urgent, assignee=self.
For MODERATE: ONE issue with checklist of all items, priority=medium, assignee=self.
For RECURRING: tag with `recurring`, priority=high, mention past memory in body.
Post created issue IDs as comment. Set task to done.

tasks.title: [{{date}}] Infra Health — Write history
description: First, update LAST WEEK's memory outcome based on what you observed this run (link from [{{read_history.identifier}}] memory ID). Use one of: `good` (predictions held, no surprises), `neutral` (mixed), `negative` (regressions, recurring issues unresolved):
node scripts/tools/pipeline-memory.mjs update-outcome-latest weekly-infrastructure-health good  # auto-finds prior run, idempotent
Then compose THIS WEEK's memory entry. Use a unique tmp file (avoid collisions on re-run):
node scripts/tools/pipeline-memory.mjs write weekly-infrastructure-health --content "$TMPFILE" --outcome pending --agent FOUNDING_ENGINEER --tag domain:infra
- Exit 4 = degraded write (NULL embedding — Ollama down). Memory was saved but is invisible to future recalls. Set task to `blocked` and notify on-call.
- Exit 2 = network/API error. Memory NOT saved. Set task to `blocked`.
- Exit 5 = file missing/stale. Re-compose and retry.
Only set task and parent to done if write exits 0.
